bib.title: rStar-Math: Small LLMs Can Master Math Reasoning with Self-Evolved Deep Thinking

question: Can small language models (1.5B-7B) reach o1-level math reasoning through MCTS test-time search and self-evolved training data, without distillation from a stronger model?
hypothesis: Step-verified, code-augmented MCTS trajectories plus a preference-pair-trained process reward model, iterated over four rounds, let SLMs self-generate data good enough for frontier math reasoning.
contributions: Code-augmented CoT data synthesis via extensive MCTS rollouts giving step-by-step verified trajectories with Q-values
Process preference model (PPM) trained on Q-value-derived preference pairs instead of Q-value regression targets
Four-round self-evolution recipe building policy SLM and PPM from scratch

method.summary: A policy SLM generates one-step code-augmented CoT candidates in MCTS; only steps whose Python executes are kept, and Q-values are back-propagated from terminal correctness. Top-Q trajectories SFT the policy, and Q-value-selected positive/negative steps train a PPM with a Bradley-Terry pairwise loss. Four rounds over 747k problems, then PPM-guided MCTS at test time.
method.task: math word-problem reasoning with test-time search (System 2)

datasets.name: Math problem set (NuminaMath, MetaMath, GPT-4 synthesized)
datasets.source: NuminaMath competition-level only, MetaMath, plus GPT-4 synthetic problems seeded from 7.5k MATH train and 3.6k AMC-AIME train
datasets.preprocessing: GPT-4 synthetic: 10 solutions generated, keep only problems with at least 3 consistent solutions; synthetic problems with trajectory accuracy under 50% removed

datasets.name: MATH-500, AIME 2024 (30 problems), AMC 2023, Olympiad Bench, College Math, GSM8K, GaokaoEn 2023

other.note: paper says 3B in Sec 4.1 and 3.8B elsewhere

models.name: PPM
models.architecture: policy model with next-token head replaced by linear layer + tanh scalar head, outputs in [-1,1]

training.objective: Policy: SFT on top-2 correct trajectories per problem by average Q-value. PPM: Bradley-Terry pairwise ranking loss, L = -1/(2x2) E[log sigma(r(x,ypos)-r(x,yneg))], 2 positive and 2 negative steps per step
training.lr_schedule: linear for Qwen; cosine for Phi3-mini; PPM schedule not stated
training.hardware: bootstrap round: 10 nodes of 8x80GB H100; rounds 2-4: 15 nodes of 4x40GB A100
training.wall_clock: bootstrap about two weeks; rounds 2-4 three days each; final round about one week

other.policy_refit: policy fine-tuned from the initial base model each round, not incrementally
other.rollouts: 16 MCTS rollouts per problem per round (8 in bootstrap); hard problems get extra 16, then 64, then 128; round 4 uses 2 tree expansions with different seeds
other.tree: max depth 16; 8 candidate nodes per step (5 in bootstrap, 16 in round 4); UCT c=2
other.orm_pqm: ORM and PQM share architecture and training parameters with PPM; PQM uses MSE on Q-values

inference.decoding: MCTS: per step 32 candidate nodes scored by PPM, 4 rollouts per step to update Q-values; final answer = trajectory with highest PPM score
inference.samples: 8 trajectories for most benchmarks, 16 for AIME/AMC; rStar-Math64 uses 64; Pass@1 reported; no seeds or repeat runs stated
inference.prompting: MCTS prompt: '<|user|>: {question} <|assistant|>: Let's think step by step and solve the problem with code.' plus previous steps; step ends with <end_of_step>

other.tokens_per_trajectory: Table 9: MATH 5453, AIME 15693, AMC 14544, Olympiad 7889, College 4503, GSM8K 3299, Gaokao 6375

metrics.name: Pass@1 accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of problems whose single selected answer is correct (for System 2 the PPM-selected trajectory)

metrics.name: Pass@N
metrics.definition: problem solved if any of N solutions is correct

baselines: Qwen2.5-Math Instruct models and Best-of-N with 72B ORM
eval.protocol: Pass@1; frontier-model numbers for MATH, AIME taken from public reports, others re-measured; Qwen Best-of-N re-evaluated on MATH-500, AIME, AMC; same number of samples as rStar-Math

prompts.text: You are a powerful agent with broad math knowledge and great python programming skills. You need to use python interpreter to do accurate calculation on math equations.

prompts.purpose: MCTS next-step prompt for policy SLM
prompts.text: <|user|>: {input question} <|assistant|>: Let's think step by step and solve the problem with code. {trajectory of previous steps}

results.claim: rStar-Math lifts Qwen2.5-Math-7B on MATH from 58.8% to 90.0% with 64 search trajectories, above o1-preview and level with o1-mini.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-Math-7B policy + 7B PPM, MCTS, 64 trajectories, Pass@1, MATH
results.quote: On the MATH benchmark, it improves Qwen2.5-Math-7B from 58.8% to 90.0% and Phi3-mini-3.8B from 41.4% to 86.4%, surpassing o1-preview by +4.5% and +0.9%.

results.claim: On AIME 2024 rStar-Math (7B) solves 53.3% of problems, 8/15 in each of AIME I and II.
results.quote: On the USA Math Olympiad (AIME), rStar-Math solves an average of 53.3% (8/15) of problems, ranking among the top 20% the brightest high school math students.

results.claim: With only 8 trajectories rStar-Math already reaches 89.4% on MATH for the 7B model.
results.quote: On MATH benchmark, with 8 search trajectories, rStar-Math boosts Qwen2.5-Math-7B from 58.8% to 89.4% and Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B from 51.2% to 87.8%.

results.claim: The 3.8B Phi3-mini policy with the same 7B PPM reaches 86.4% on MATH (64 traj).
results.setup: Phi3-mini-Instruct fine-tuned on round-4 Qwen trajectories, 7B PPM, 64 trajectories
results.table: Table 5, row rStar-Math64 (3.8B SLM+7B PPM), column MATH

results.claim: Best-of-N with a 72B ORM on the same Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct policy gets 88.4% on MATH and 26.7% on AIME, below rStar-Math with a 7B PPM.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct + 72B ORM, Best-of-N, same number of samples
results.table: Table 5, row Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct+72B ORM, column MATH

results.claim: Self-evolution improves the policy SLM across rounds on MATH from 69.6 (r1) to 78.4 (r4) and on AIME 2024 from 3.3 to 26.7 (greedy Pass@1).
results.setup: Qwen2.5-Math-7B fine-tuned each round from base, greedy Pass@1
results.table: Table 3, row policy SLM-r4, column MATH

results.setup: Qwen2.5-Math-7B, System 2 inference, 8 trajectories (16 for AIME/AMC)

results.setup: Policy fixed to policy SLM-r1, PPM-r1..r4

results.claim: Share of the 747k problems solved in training set rises from 60.17% (round 1) to 90.25% (round 4); Olympiad-level from 20.99% to 80.58%.
Step-by-step verified trajectories as SFT data beat GPT-4 distillation (MetaMath, NuminaMath-CoT), random self-generation and ORM rejection sampling.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-Math-7B SFT, same recipe, MATH Pass@1
results.note: baseline is rejection sampling; NuminaMath-CoT 69.6, random sample 72.4, MetaMath 55.2
results.table: Table 7, row Step-by-step verified (ours), column MATH

results.claim: PPM beats an outcome reward model (Best-of-N) and a Q-value regression PRM (PQM) when guiding search.
results.setup: Round-4 policy, MCTS (PQM, PPM) vs Best-of-N (ORM), MATH
results.note: ORM 82.6, PQM 88.2, PPM 89.4. AIME: ORM 26.7, PQM 46.7, PPM 50.0.

results.claim: The reward model dominates final performance: despite differing Pass@1, final accuracy of the three policy sizes converges under the PPM.
results.quote: Moreover, despite varying Pass@1 accuracy across our three policy SLM sizes, the final reasoning accuracy converges after applying the PPM.

results.claim: Self-reflection emerges unprompted: the policy backtracks from low-quality steps to a simpler solution.
results.setup: Qualitative example (Fig 4) and one more in Appendix A.2; no self-reflection data or prompt
results.quote: Notably, no self-reflection training data or prompt was included, suggesting that advanced System 2 reasoning can foster intrinsic self-reflection.

results.claim: Inference is token-heavy: MCTS generates on average 15693 tokens per trajectory on AIME 2024 and 5453 on MATH.
results.setup: Average generated tokens per trajectory, MCTS inference

results.claim: Self-evolution data generation cost: bootstrap round took about two weeks on 10 nodes of 8x80GB H100; rounds 2-4 took three days each on 15 nodes of 4x40GB A100 (round 4 about one week).
results.quote: This required approximately two weeks to finish the data generation.

results.claim: PPM-fine-tuned policy models do not beat official Instruct versions on Pass@1 (e.g. 78.4 vs 82.6 on MATH for Qwen2.5-Math-7B).
results.quote: Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct achieves 4.2% higher accuracy on the MATH benchmark.

limits: Four rounds of self-evolution run only on Qwen2.5-Math-7B due to limited GPU; other three policies are fine-tuned on its round-4 data and reuse its PPM.
Geometry problems needing visual understanding are unsupported; 8 unsolved AIME problems were geometry-based.
Accuracy saturates or slows at 64 trajectories on MATH, AIME and Olympiad Bench.
Needs problems with ground-truth final answers; extending to code or general reasoning requires a feedback mechanism (test cases, human labels, mutual verification).
Remaining unsolved synthetic problems are largely mislabeled (19 of 20 sampled), so self-evolution stopped at 90.25% coverage.
Inference is expensive: thousands of tokens per trajectory, 8 to 64 trajectories, with 32 candidates per step.

Benchmark numbers for o1/Claude/QwQ partly from public reports, not re-measured; no seeds, variance or significance tests; no ablation of the code-execution filter alone; frontier-model comparisons are with default settings.
Fine-tuned policies do not beat official Instruct models on Pass@1.

terms.definition: process preference model: a reward model trained with Q-value-based positive/negative step pairs and a pairwise ranking loss rather than score regression
Q-value-based process reward model trained with MSE on Q-values as labels
